title: Why Battlestar Galactica Still Defines 2000s Sci-Fi
excerpt:
A new retrospective calls Battlestar Galactica the decade's best show.
Its political and religious themes remain central to its reputation.
body_md:
Ronald D. Moore and David Eick reimagined Battlestar Galactica as a grounded science-fiction drama about humanity's survival after a devastating Cylon attack. Rather than relying on conventional space-opera spectacle, the series explored military command, democratic legitimacy, faith, and moral compromise.

Edward James Olmos, Mary McDonnell, Katee Sackhoff and Tricia Helfer helped bring the conflicted survivors to life. Their fleet searches for Earth while facing threats from both outside and within. The show drew on the political atmosphere after September 11 and the War on Terror, often questioning the assumptions behind the era's security debates.

A recent opinion piece argues that this combination makes the reboot the defining television drama of the 2000s. That superlative is the author's assessment, not an official ranking, and the series' conclusion remains divisive among some viewers.
